properties.name: Bradbury Landing
properties.description: Curiosity's landing site (August 2012) on the floor of Gale crater. Flat, well-mapped ground makes it the natural base and start point for walking EVAs.

properties.name: Yellowknife Bay (John Klein drill site)
properties.description: First rock drilled on Mars. The mudstone showed that an ancient lake here could have supported microbial life: water, key elements and an energy source.

properties.name: The Kimberley (Windjana)
properties.description: Sandstone outcrops where Curiosity drilled Windjana and found unusual potassium-rich minerals. Good place to study how Gale's sediments were delivered.

properties.name: Pahrump Hills
properties.description: Base of Mount Sharp. Layered lake mudstones of the Murray formation record how long liquid water persisted in Gale crater.

properties.name: Murray Buttes
properties.description: Mesas capped by wind-deposited sandstone. A scenic stop that shows the dry, windy climate that followed the lake era.

properties.name: Vera Rubin Ridge
properties.description: Erosion-resistant ridge rich in hematite. Studying it explains how groundwater altered the rocks after the lake dried out.

properties.name: Glen Torridon (clay-bearing unit)
properties.description: Clay minerals detected from orbit, confirmed by Curiosity's drill. Clays preserve organic molecules well, a priority target for astronauts.

properties.name: Mont Mercou
properties.description: Cliff at the transition from clay-bearing to sulfate-bearing layers: a record of Mars changing from a wetter to a drier world.
